title: Restore the workshop discovery
instructions: Read the complete passage before answering. Enter exactly one word in each gap. Complete all eight gaps before checking the passage.

parts.prompt: Gap 1: enter the article required before “unopened wooden box”.

response.rationale: The singular countable noun is introduced for the first time, and “unopened” begins with a vowel sound, so the article is “an”.

parts.hint: The box is mentioned for the first time. Say the phrase aloud and listen to the first sound in “unopened”.
parts.correct_explanation: “An unopened wooden box” uses the indefinite article “an” before a vowel sound.

parts.prompt: Gap 2: enter the pronoun that refers to the wooden box.

response.rationale: The object pronoun “it” refers back to the singular inanimate noun “box”.

parts.hint: Replace the repeated words “the wooden box” with one object pronoun.
parts.correct_explanation: “It” is the object pronoun that refers back to the singular wooden box.

parts.prompt: Gap 3: enter the auxiliary that completes the past-perfect verb phrase.

response.rationale: Packing happened before the later donation and workshop discovery, and “packed” is a past participle, so “had packed” completes the past-perfect phrase.

parts.hint: The packing happened before the box was donated and discovered. Complete “___ packed”.
parts.correct_explanation: “Had packed” places the earlier packing before the later events in the narrative.

parts.prompt: Gap 4: enter the preposition that completes “tied ___ a ribbon”.

response.rationale: The established pattern is “tie something with” the material used to fasten it.

parts.hint: The ribbon is the material used to fasten the letters.
parts.correct_explanation: The letters were “tied with” a ribbon because the ribbon was used to fasten them.

parts.prompt: Gap 5: enter the conjunction that contrasts fragile paper with clear writing.

response.rationale: “Although” and the approved alternative “though” introduce a concession: the paper was fragile, yet the writing remained clear.

parts.hint: The two facts are surprising together: the paper was fragile, but the writing remained clear.
parts.correct_explanation: “Although” introduces the contrast between the paper's condition and the clarity of its writing; “though” is also accepted.

parts.prompt: Gap 6: enter the relative word required after the comma.

response.rationale: The comma begins a non-defining relative clause about the concert, which requires “which” rather than “that”.

parts.hint: The words after the comma add extra information about the concert in a non-defining relative clause.
parts.correct_explanation: “Which” correctly introduces the non-defining relative clause after the comma.

parts.prompt: Gap 7: enter the conjunction that marks the end point of the waiting.

response.rationale: “Until” and the approved alternative “till” introduce the event that ended the audience's wait.

parts.hint: The lights returning marks the moment when the audience stopped waiting.
parts.correct_explanation: The audience waited “until” the lights returned; “till” is also accepted.

parts.prompt: Gap 8: enter the pronoun that refers to the letters.

response.rationale: The plural subject pronoun “they” refers back to the letters and controls the plural verb “connected”.

parts.hint: Use a plural subject pronoun for the letters mentioned throughout the passage.
parts.correct_explanation: “They” refers back to the plural noun “letters” and serves as the subject of “connected”.
